title: MigrateBatchNFTMinter lacks a chainid guard, unlike its sibling funder
description: MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol run() (lines 114-140) executes the migration without a fail-fast network guard. The sibling cluster script MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter.s.sol pins `require(block.chainid == 1, ...)` at line 289, and the repo's Configuration-Safety convention mandates such a guard, but it is absent here. A broadcast against the wrong chain is not fail-fast at entry.
impact: NONE in practice. A broadcast against the wrong chain would almost certainly revert on the first external call to a non-existent contract (the script uses hardcoded mainnet addresses), and the broadcast itself requires a Ledger signature. This is a Configuration-Safety / cluster-consistency nit, not a demonstrated exploit path or asset-impact finding.
attackPath: No attacker path. Self-inflicted operator misconfiguration only:
1. Operator points --rpc-url / --fork-url at a non-mainnet chain (fat-finger or stale env).
2. run() executes without a chainid fail-fast guard.
3. Execution almost always reverts on the first call to an address with no code on the wrong chain; nothing material happens.
recommendation: Add `require(block.chainid == 1, "expected mainnet (1)")` at the top of run() (or gate behind PREVIEW for local), matching the sibling MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter.s.sol:289 and the repo Configuration-Safety gate.

poc.note: Low/QA severity; no coded PoC required. Self-defeating mitigations (RPC pin + Ledger sig + hardcoded mainnet addresses + reverts-on-wrong-chain) and no demonstrated exploit path.

classification.reasoning: Confirmed Low/QA. Configuration-Safety / cluster-consistency nit: a cheap standard fail-fast guard the rest of the cluster relies on (sibling pins block.chainid==1) and the repo Configuration-Safety section mandates, but its absence here has self-defeating mitigations and no demonstrated HM exploit path or asset impact. Per CLAUDE.md, missing standard guards with no HM exploit path are QA/Low at best.
